newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint eases vs dlr, BCE mark futures most traded.
newsitem.headline: Forint eases vs dlr, BCE mark futures most traded.

text.p: The Hungarian forint closed a quiet session slightly weaker against the dollar, dealers said.
"I have the feeling that many people are still on vacation," said Istvan Gere of ING Bank.
The forint closed at 150.72/77 to the U.S. unit compared with its opening of 150.65/70, and remained some five pips weaker than the central bank bid.

On the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), German mark contracts accounted for half the total 973 million forint currency futures turnover, followed by the dollar, with smaller amounts of Ecu and lira changing hands.
The two most popular currency futures were also the main movers, the mark rising and the dollar dropping for most maturities.
Sterling and Ecu futures also rose for one maturity each.
